> **This project contains synthetic data and analysis created for demonstration purposes only.**
> Beacon Point Emergency Management Agency is fictional. Every incident, response and comment was generated by AI.

## Purpose

The Continuous Improvement Office asks every deployed staff member to complete a short
post-deployment survey, and AAR teams record strengths and areas for improvement after each
incident. This report combines the two sources to answer three questions:

1. **Where is the deployment experience weakest, and is it getting better?**
2. **Who is having a harder time?** Which roles, regions or first-time deployers?
3. **What are people writing about?** Recurring themes in open-text comments and AAR observations,
   found with transparent, repeatable text methods (no generative AI).

## The data

```{r load-data}
ci <- load_ci_data()
responses <- ci$responses
incidents <- ci$incidents
aar <- ci$aar
```

```{r data-summary}
tibble(
  Dataset = c("Incidents", "Survey responses", "Survey comments", "AAR observations"),
  Rows = c(nrow(incidents), nrow(responses), sum(!is.na(responses$comment)), nrow(aar)),
  Covers = c(
    paste(min(incidents$start_date), "to", max(incidents$start_date)),

) |>

```

## 1. Where is the experience weakest?

```{r likert, fig.height = 4.2}
likert <- responses |>
  select(response_id, starts_with("score_")) |>
  pivot_longer(-response_id, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "score") |>
  filter(!is.na(score)) |>
  count(dimension, score) |>
  group_by(dimension) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n), top2 = sum(pct[score >= 4])) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    label = SCORE_LABELS[dimension],
    label = fct_reorder(label, top2),
    score = factor(score, levels = 5:1)
  )

top2_labels <- likert |> distinct(label, top2)

ggplot(likert, aes(pct, label, fill = score)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    data = top2_labels, aes(x = 1.02, y = label, label = percent(top2, 1)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, size = 3.6, color = "#52514E"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = likert_colors(), breaks = as.character(1:5),
    labels = c("1 Very poor", "2 Poor", "3 Acceptable", "4 Good", "5 Excellent"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(
    title = "Lodging & logistics and tools & technology trail every other area",
    subtitle = "Share of responses at each rating; right-hand figure is % rating Good or Excellent",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Is it getting better?

The new mobile field kits were issued agency-wide on **July 1, 2025**. Tools & technology
scores moved more than any other dimension after that date.

```{r trend}
trend <- responses |>
  filter(submitted_at < as.Date("2026-10-01")) |> # complete quarters only
  group_by(quarter) |>
  summarise(across(c(score_tools_tech, score_communication, score_logistics, score_onboarding), mean)) |>
  pivot_longer(-quarter, names_to = "dimension", values_to = "avg") |>
  mutate(label = SCORE_LABELS[dimension])

# Direct labels at the line ends, nudged apart so close values don't overlap
end_labels <- trend |>
  filter(quarter == max(quarter)) |>
  arrange(avg) |>
  mutate(label_y = avg)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(end_labels))[-1]) {
  end_labels$label_y[i] <- max(end_labels$label_y[i], end_labels$label_y[i - 1] + 0.11)
}

ggplot(trend, aes(quarter, avg, color = label, group = label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = "2025 Q3", color = "#C9C8C2", linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = "2025 Q3", y = 2.35, label = "  Field kit rollout", hjust = 0, size = 3.4, color = "#52514E") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, color = "white", stroke = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  geom_text(data = end_labels, aes(y = label_y, label = label), hjust = -0.08, size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = ci_series_colors(4), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(2.2, 4.2)) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 3.2))) +
  labs(
    title = "Tools & technology jumped a full point after the field kit rollout",
    subtitle = "Average rating (1-5) by quarter",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## 2. Who is having a harder time?

```{r region-heatmap, fig.height = 4.2}
region_scores <- responses |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(across(score_onboarding:score_leadership, mean), n = n()) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("score_"), names_to = "dimension", values_to = "avg") |>
  mutate(label = factor(SCORE_LABELS[dimension], levels = SCORE_LABELS))

ggplot(region_scores, aes(label, region, fill = avg)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = number(avg, 0.1)), size = 3.8, color = "#14171C") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#C93A39", mid = "#F0EFEC", high = "#1C5CAB", midpoint = 3.3,
    limits = c(2, 4.2), name = "Avg rating"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = label_wrap(14)) +
  labs(
    title = "Gulf Coast hurricane deployments drive the logistics problem",
    subtitle = "Average rating by region (1-5)",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
```

```{r first-deployment, fig.height = 3.4}
responses |>

  labs(

  ) +

  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Does experience predict retention?

```{r redeploy, fig.height = 3.6}
responses |>
  filter(!is.na(score_overall)) |>
  group_by(score_overall) |>
  summarise(pct_yes = mean(would_redeploy == "Yes"), n = n()) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(score_overall), pct_yes)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, fill = ci_series_colors(1)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct_yes, 1)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(
    title = "Staff who rate their deployment 4 or 5 are far more likely to volunteer again",
    subtitle = "% answering 'Yes' to 'Would you volunteer to deploy again?', by overall rating",
    x = "Overall experience rating", y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## 3. What are people writing about?

Every method in this section is **deterministic and explainable**: the same text always
produces the same result, and each result can be traced back to specific words. Analysts review
and name the themes; the methods only surface patterns for a human to judge.

### Most frequent words

```{r top-words, fig.height = 4.5}
comment_tokens <- tokenize_text(responses, response_id, comment)

top_words <- comment_tokens |>
  count(word, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 15)

top_words |>
  mutate(word = fct_reorder(word, n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, word)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, fill = ci_series_colors(1)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(n)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(
      "\"", top_words$word[1], "\", \"", top_words$word[2], "\" and \"",
      top_words$word[3], "\" come up most in open-text comments"
    ),
    subtitle = "Most frequent words in survey comments, after removing common words",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Themes across all text (topic model)

A topic model groups words that tend to appear together. It was trained on all survey comments
and AAR observations by `ml/train_model.R` with a fixed random seed, so it gives the same
answer every time. Topic names were proposed from keyword lists and confirmed by an analyst.

```{r topics, fig.height = 6}
if (!file.exists(MODEL_PATH())) source("ml/train_model.R", local = new.env())
model <- readRDS(MODEL_PATH())

model$top_terms |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(beta, n = 7, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(term = reorder_within(term, beta, label)) |>
  ggplot(aes(beta, term)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, fill = ci_series_colors(1)) +
  facet_wrap(~label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  labs(
    title = "Six recurring themes in deployment feedback",
    subtitle = "Top words per topic; longer bar = more characteristic of the topic",
    x = "Word probability within topic", y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

```{r topic-by-region}
model$doc_topics |>
  inner_join(select(responses, response_id, region), by = c("doc_id" = "response_id")) |>
  count(region, topic_label) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = topic_label, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "region") |>
  fmt_percent(-region, decimals = 0) |>
  data_color(
    columns = -region, palette = c("#FFFFFF", "#86B6EF", "#1C5CAB"), domain = c(0, 0.6)
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Which themes each region writes about",
    subtitle = "Share of a region's survey comments assigned to each topic"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(SYNTHETIC_CAPTION)
```

### Do hurricanes generate different problems?

```{r topic-by-hazard, fig.height = 4.2}
hazard_mix <- model$doc_topics |>
  inner_join(aar, by = c("doc_id" = "aar_id")) |>
  filter(section == "Area for Improvement") |>
  mutate(group = if_else(incident_type == "Hurricane", "Hurricanes", "All other incidents")) |>
  count(group, topic_label) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

hurricane_top <- hazard_mix |>
  filter(group == "Hurricanes") |>
  slice_max(pct, n = 1)

hazard_mix |>
  mutate(
    topic_label = fct_reorder(topic_label, pct * (group == "Hurricanes"), sum),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Hurricanes", "All other incidents"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, topic_label, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7, color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = percent(pct, 1)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ci_series_colors(2), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Hurricane AARs flag ", tolower(hurricane_top$topic_label), " more than any other theme"),
    subtitle = "Share of AAR 'areas for improvement' assigned to each topic",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = SYNTHETIC_CAPTION
  ) +
  theme_ci() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Finding similar past observations

When a new issue comes in, analysts can check whether it has been seen before. The similarity
search compares word usage (TF-IDF cosine similarity: words that are rare across all
observations count for more than common ones) and shows the shared words behind
each match, so the reason for every match is visible.

```{r similarity}
query <- "The night shift never got a handoff briefing and repeated the day team's work"

find_similar(model, query, n = 5) |>
  left_join(select(aar, aar_id, incident_name, section, observation), by = "aar_id") |>
  select(incident_name, section, observation, shared_words, similarity) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(similarity, decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(
    incident_name = "Incident", section = "Type", observation = "Past AAR observation",
    shared_words = "Matched on", similarity = "Similarity"
  ) |>
  tab_header(title = "Past AAR observations most similar to:", subtitle = md(paste0("*", query, "*"))) |>
  tab_source_note(SYNTHETIC_CAPTION)
```

## Key findings

```{r findings, include = FALSE}
pre_tech <- mean(responses$score_tools_tech[responses$submitted_at < as.Date("2025-07-01")])
post_tech <- mean(responses$score_tools_tech[responses$submitted_at >= as.Date("2025-07-01")])
gulf_log <- mean(responses$score_logistics[responses$region == "Gulf Coast"])
other_log <- mean(responses$score_logistics[responses$region != "Gulf Coast"])
onb <- responses |> group_by(first_deployment) |> summarise(m = mean(score_onboarding))
```

1. **The field kit rollout worked.** Tools & technology rose from `r number(pre_tech, 0.1)` to
   `r number(post_tech, 0.1)` after July 2025. Use this as the model for measuring other fixes.
2. **Gulf Coast logistics needs a plan before hurricane season.** Logistics averages
   `r number(gulf_log, 0.1)` in the Gulf Coast versus `r number(other_log, 0.1)` elsewhere, and
   lodging and logistics is the most common theme in hurricane AARs.
3. **First-time deployers need more onboarding support.** They rate onboarding
   `r number(onb$m[onb$first_deployment == "Yes"], 0.1)` versus
   `r number(onb$m[onb$first_deployment == "No"], 0.1)` for experienced staff. A mentor program
   is the most common recommendation in the AARs.
4. **Experience drives retention.** Staff who rate a deployment 4 or 5 are much more likely to
   volunteer again, so these fixes are a workforce issue as well as a satisfaction issue.
